html:
Abyssinia is the old European name for Ethiopia, used on the map in its 1914 snapshot for the Ethiopian Empire. In 1914 it was one of only two African states, with Liberia, still independent of European rule.

That independence was won at the Battle of Adwa in 1896, when Emperor Menelik II crushed an Italian army. Menelik had also doubled the empire's size by conquering the lands to the south and east, and founded the new capital Addis Ababa. A railway from French Djibouti was climbing toward it.

Menelik died in December 1913. His grandson Lij Iyasu ruled uncrowned, but his ties to Muslims and to the Central Powers in World War I alarmed the nobles and the church, and they deposed him in 1916. Menelik's daughter Zewditu became empress, with Ras Tafari, later Haile Selassie, as regent and heir.
sum: Abyssinia is the old European name for Ethiopia, used on the map in its 1914 snapshot for the Ethiopian Empire. In 1914 it was one of only two African states, with Liberia, still independent of European rule.
